thread:
mei: hey team — following the Node quickstart in a Docker image and my first API call is failing with an HTML 502. same token used from Console works. any ideas?

mei: command: `docker run --rm -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_API_KEY redwood/sample-node-quickstart`

mei: response:
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: text/html

<html>502 Bad Gateway</html>
```

owen: is that a workspace token or service key? 502 usually points to a gateway/proxy, not auth.

mei: workspace token from Console -> Settings. i tried a service key and saw 403 inside the container. workspace token gave the 502.

devex-bot: Tip: if you see different responses from host vs container, check for intermediate proxies or container runtime networking. Some proxies strip Authorization headers.

own: try curl from your host with the same token: `curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"input":"hi"}'`

mei: host curl returns 402 JSON: `{"error":"org_billing_required","help":"https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/acme/billing"}`. inside Docker it's the HTML 502.

own: that suggests a header removal on the container/network path. when Auth is removed the SDK may retry and some frontends return HTML 502s instead of JSON 401/402. awkward DX.

onboard-bot: Notice: Your org (acme) currently has no billing method. First outbound requests can be blocked. Add billing at https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/acme/billing :credit_card:

mei: dashboard quickstart didn't surface the billing modal for me which is why i assumed token acceptance. mismatch between control plane UI and runtime gating is confusing.

own: short-term workaround: mount a service key file into the container and set REDWOOD_API_KEY by reading it (bypass some proxy header rewrites). also try `--network=host` to rule out daemon-level proxies.

mei: mounted service key file and reran; got the 402 JSON with `org_billing_required`. confirmed.

own: action items: 1) devex to add a preflight billing check in the CLI quickstart that prints an explicit billing hint before making requests; 2) SDK/CLI should detect common 502 patterns caused by missing Authorization and show an actionable message mapping to billing/auth; 3) docs: note that some corporate/container networks may strip Authorization and recommend secret-file mounts.

mei: filing eng/devex ticket with minimal Dockerfile, host vs container curl traces, and run commands. tagging @owen. thanks! :pray:
